newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Irish police question two over Plantier murder.
newsitem.headline: Irish police question two over Plantier murder.

text.p: Irish police detained a man and a woman for questioning on Monday over the December murder of Sophie Toscan du Plantier, wife of a French film producer.
The two were arrested separately and taken for questioning at police headquarters in Bandon, one of West Cork's major towns, before midday, police said.
Police sources said the two were arrested in the neighbourhood of Schull, close to the village where the French woman was found dead on December 23.
She had been bludgeoned to death in a lane near her West Cork holiday home at Dunmanuf three days after arriving from France to take a brief vacation.
The 38-year-old woman was married to Daniel Toscan du Plantier, a leading figure in the French film world and a friend of French President Jacques Chirac.
The pair can be held for up to 12 hours without being charged under Irish law.
The man was arrested in the morning and the woman was detained a few hours later, police said.
Irish media said neither was an Irish national but police declined to give any details.
The arrests follow one of the biggest international investigations carried out by Irish police, who visited France on several occasions for talks with their French counterparts.
The killing threw the media spotlight on the West Cork region, home to hundreds of expatriates drawn by its stunning unspoilt beauty and remoteness.
Many have gravitated towards the region of Schull which has spectacular ocean views, a thriving harbour where foreign yachts are moored and few rural houses.
House prices in the West Cork region have risen by up to 20 percent in the past two years because of growing foreign demand for secluded residences, estage agents say.
Du Plantier and his wife had a small house in Dunmanuf village and were infrequent visitors in recent years.
Germans, Belgians, French, Danes and Swedes are among many of the nationalities who have settled in the region.
West Cork is principally an agricultural region but its economy has benefited from huge foreign tourist interest since the mid 1970s, local officials say.
